# Autonomous quantum protection with physical small-qubit controllers

2026-11-01. Ordinary proof and code package. This extends, rather than replaces, the previously delivered noisy-witness memory construction.

## What was constructed

At the specified engineered Lindblad-generator level, syndrome acquisition and classical correction now run autonomously using operations on at most six physical qubits at a time. The clocks, probes, cached syndrome bits, Boolean wires and correction flags are included as noisy physical systems. There is no trusted external timing service, perfectly reliable collision flag, or primitive that directly reads an entire stabilizer.

The key change is to allow probes to overlap and produce wrong reports. An exact finite-clock Poisson potential pays their actual overlap occupation. A separate physical sorting process repairs malformed clock states. These mechanisms join the earlier protected-memory proof with a strictly positive, size-independent formal noise-admission region. The whole mathematical join received a separate internal review; the review's assumptions and limitations are included.

## Meaning and limits

This removes an essential implementation assumption from the formal autonomous-memory route. It is NOT a civilisation-level breakthrough, a practical quantum-memory demonstration, an economical threshold, or a proved advantage over active correction with the same hardware.

The construction still requires the particular admitted Tanner-code family, finite but potentially enormous apparatus and rate constants, non-Euclidean code wiring, actual reset/readout reservoirs, ideal encoded input and ideal terminal decoding. The local six-qubit dissipative operations are specified engineered primitives; a microscopic two-body Hamiltonian/reservoir realization is not supplied by this theorem. Physical errors of the faster repair apparatus must satisfy the actual bound after all rates are chosen.

## Read in this order

1. `NATIVE_DILUTE_SENSOR_MEMORY_JOIN.md`: complete joined theorem, physical primitives, rate hierarchy, protected logical interface and output bound.
2. `audits/NATIVE_DILUTE_SENSOR_WHOLE_RECEIPT.md`: separate whole-theorem review, including exact scope.
3. `construction/07_dilute_sensor_closed_join.md`: explicit source/Boolean prices and rate-density inequalities.
4. `construction/FLAG_FREE_SOURCE_ADMISSION.md`

This note is a prior comparison, not an audit certifying them. No forbidden source was retrieved. All new accesses succeeded.

## Closest prior contracts

**DST, Quantum Memory and Autonomous Computation in Two Dimensions, arXiv2601.20818v3 (25 Sep 2026).** https://arxiv.org/html/2601.20818v3 . Supplement formal Theorem1 proves the synchronous dissipative QCA threshold with sufficiently correct encoded input and composable local fault strength; noisy internal classical organization is not simply ignored. Main text continuous-time section explicitly leaves its threshold extension for future work (line124), repeated at Supplement VII opening (line1717). VII.1 discusses finite marching-soldier clocks, winding deadlock and local repair; VII.2 sketches continuous-time operation. Therefore its autonomous continuous-time architecture is strong prior, but it is not an established theorem with the candidate's actual continuously noisy physical sensors/clocks. Removing the unproved clock-to-faultpath bridge would matter; no claim that autonomous architecture itself is new.

**Midha–Abanin, Local autonomous inference machines for quantum LDPC codes, arXiv2609.38139v1 (29 Sep 2026).** https://arxiv.org/html/2609.38139v1 . Discussion explicitly confines the results to offline decoding: errors sampled once, no subsequent noise. Online syndrome/fault ingress is future work. Local BP processing and autonomous feedback therefore do not supply a perpetually noisy live decoder service. The proposed sensor/compiler contract is materially stronger on this axis.

**Gu et al., Single-Shot Decoding of Good Quantum LDPC Codes, CMP405,85 (14 Mar 2024).** https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00220-024-04951-6 . Thm3.4: residual reduced weight bounded by alpha times old error plus beta times syndrome noise; parallel k iterations achieve alpha=2^{-Omega(k)}. Thm3.5 and Cor3.6 already prove repeated fresh-syndrome recovery with constant iterations and exponentially suppressed per-round tails. Purpose-bounded primary-source check for the fixed finite witness memory compiler. No assertion of historical novelty. No forbidden sources retrieved, no access failure in this pass.

## Verdict
No inspected theorem supplies the requested fixed-rate, noisy-auxiliary, low-arity compiler preserving exponential lifetime. There ARE older phase-preserving Hamiltonian gadgets and time-uniform dissipative stability theorems: do not describe all prior as merely finite-time simulation. Their contracts do not join to the requested nonequilibrium memory automatically.

## Closest actual contracts

Proposition27/28, Eqs54–65: nonunitary locality reduction, ancilla measured every δt; effective channel error O(t δt), unwanted ancilla branch O(t δt²); interactions include O(δt^-1/2) and O(δt^-1). Thus exponential target time forces shrinking step/increasing strength under this guarantee. Discussion explicitly notes precisely engineered stroboscopic dissipation and multiple-gadget ancilla accumulation. Their generic Hamiltonian simulation lower bounds are NOT a no-go for phase-specific protection.
